question.problem: A container with $\frac{3}{4}$ gallons of weed killer can spray $\frac{7}{4}$ lawns. What is the unit rate of gallons per lawn?
question.worked_solution:
To compute the unit rate of gallons per lawn, we divide the number of gallons, $\frac{3}{4},$ by the number of lawns, $\frac{7}{4}$, as follows: 

$$
\frac{3}{4}÷\frac{7}{4}
$$

Dividing a fraction by another fraction is equivalent to multiplying the first fraction by the reciprocal of the second fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}÷\frac{7}{4} & =\frac{3}{4}\times \frac{4}{7} \\  & =\frac{3\times 4}{4\times 7} \\  & =\frac{3\times \cancel{4}}{\cancel{4}\times 7} \\  & =\frac{3}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit rate is $\frac{3}{7}$ gallons per lawn.
